title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Imricor Personnel
tiers.description: All directors and officers, all direct reports to the CEO, all other personnel (employees and contractors), and family members/trusts/bodies corporate over whom such a person has or may reasonably be expected to have investment control or influence.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: All directors and other key management personnel (AASB 124), any other person designated by the Board, and their family members/trusts/bodies corporate with investment control or influence; subject to Blackout Periods, blanket year-round clearance, and the short-term trading ban.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Imricor; within Designated Persons, distinguished for clearance (from the Chairman) and the ASX notification duty for changes in relevant interests.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman; within Designated Persons, distinguished because their own trading is cleared by the Board rather than the Chairman.

tiers.name: employees (Designated Persons who are not directors)
tiers.description: Designated Persons who are KMP or Board-nominated but not directors; cleared by the Chief Executive Officer.

definitions.hedging_definition: any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value attaching to the relevant securities and remove the element of price risk inherent in the value of those securities

windows.start_anchor: two weeks before the end of a half-year
windows.end_anchor: two trading days after release of Imricor's half-year financial results to ASX

windows.start_anchor: two weeks before the end of a financial year
windows.end_anchor: two trading days after release of Imricor's annual financial results to ASX

windows.start_anchor: two weeks before the end of the first and third quarters of a financial year (while quarterly cash flow reporting is required)
windows.end_anchor: two trading days after release of the cash flow report to ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may, from time to time, declare any other relevant period to be a Blackout Period or determine that a period will not be one, and may vary the opening or closing date of any Blackout Period; the CEO or CFO notifies Designated Persons of the precise dates. No confidentiality obligation is stated for the fact of an additional Blackout Period.

rules.detail: Securities covered by the policy expressly include derivative products issued over or in respect of Imricor securities, cash-settled or otherwise; Trading in them is permitted for general Imricor Personnel subject only to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: derivative products issued over or in respect of any of the above (e.g. swaps, futures, hedges, and options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Designated Persons must obtain prior written clearance for all Trading, including in derivative products, at all times (not only during Blackout Periods, where clearance is limited to exceptional circumstances).
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may trade in Imricor securities outside of Blackout Periods if they obtain prior written clearance

rules.detail: Writing forward contracts or put or call options over, or trading derivative products in respect of, plan securities is prohibited while those securities remain unvested or subject to escrow, for any holder (not only Designated Persons).
rules.evidence: Prohibited conduct includes writing forward contracts or put or call options over the underlying securities, trading in derivative products or entering into other arrangements intended to hedge a "profit" in those securities

rules.detail: Once vesting/escrow ends, any holder of the relevant securities (Designated Person or not) may undertake a forward/put/call/derivative transaction of the kind described in section 6.2, provided they obtain written clearance under sections 5.3 and 5.4.
rules.evidence: After vesting and the cessation of any applicable escrow arrangements, a holder of the relevant securities may undertake any transaction of a type referred to in this section provided they obtain written clearance in the manner described in sections 5.3 and 5.4

rules.detail: Plan participants and anyone else holding securities subject to vesting conditions or escrow are prohibited from any conduct that secures the economic value of, and removes price risk from, those securities while unvested.
rules.evidence: All participants in an approved share or option plan of Imricor or who otherwise hold securities in Imricor which are subject to performance or other vesting conditions or escrow are prohibited from engaging in any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value attaching to the relevant securities and remove the element of price risk inherent in the value of those securities, while the securities remain unvested or subject to escrow.

rules.detail: The ban extends to securities that have vested but remain subject to an escrow arrangement, treated equivalently to unvested securities.
rules.evidence: while the securities remain unvested or subject to escrow

rules.detail: After vesting and cessation of escrow, hedging-type transactions become permitted for any holder, subject to prior written clearance under 5.3/5.4 and compliance with the rest of the policy (including timing rules).
rules.evidence: After vesting and the cessation of any applicable escrow arrangements, a holder of the relevant securities may undertake any transaction of a type referred to in this section provided they obtain written clearance in the manner described in sections 5.3 and 5.4 and comply with all applicable laws

rules.detail: Writing a forward contract over unvested or escrowed plan securities (a form of monetisation) is expressly prohibited conduct.
rules.evidence: Prohibited conduct includes writing forward contracts or put or call options over the underlying securities

rules.detail: Once vested and out of escrow, a forward-sale style monetisation of the relevant securities is permitted with clearance under 5.3/5.4; a monetisation of ordinary open-market shares never subject to vesting/escrow is not captured by 6.2 and instead falls under the general Trading rules for the holder's tier.
rules.evidence: After vesting and the cessation of any applicable escrow arrangements, a holder of the relevant securities may undertake any transaction of a type referred to in this section provided they obtain written clearance

rules.detail: Short selling is not named; only 'short-term' trading (a holding-period concept, section 6.1) is addressed, and only for Designated Persons.

Stock lending arrangements affecting Imricor securities are expressly listed as 'Trading in securities' under the general definition, permitted for general Imricor Personnel subject to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Trading in securities includes: ... stock lending arrangements affecting Imricor securities.

rules.detail: As a form of Trading, stock lending by Designated Persons requires the same year-round prior written clearance as any other Trading.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may trade in Imricor securities outside of Blackout Periods if they obtain prior written clearance

rules.detail: Pledging, lending or using unvested or escrowed plan securities as collateral is expressly prohibited conduct.
rules.evidence: a margin loan or similar funding arrangement or other financial transaction which can give rise to pledging, lending or using the securities as collateral

rules.detail: Once vested and out of escrow, lending/pledging arrangements over the relevant securities are permitted with 5.3/5.4 clearance.
rules.evidence: After vesting and the cessation of any applicable escrow arrangements, a holder of the relevant securities may undertake any transaction of a type referred to in this section provided they obtain written clearance

rules.detail: CFDs are not named, but are caught as cash-settled derivative products issued in respect of Imricor securities within the general Securities/Trading definition.
rules.evidence: derivative products issued over or in respect of any of the above (e.g. swaps, futures, hedges, and options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: As a cash-settled derivative product, a CFD referencing Imricor securities is Trading requiring the Designated Person's year-round clearance.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may trade in Imricor securities outside of Blackout Periods if they obtain prior written clearance

rules.detail: Acquiring or disposing of Imricor securities in connection with margin lending is expressly listed as Trading, permitted for general Imricor Personnel subject to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Trading in securities includes: ... acquiring or disposing of Imricor securities in connection with margin lending or other security arrangement

rules.detail: Margin lending Trading by Designated Persons requires the same year-round prior written clearance as any other Trading.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may trade in Imricor securities outside of Blackout Periods if they obtain prior written clearance

rules.detail: A margin loan or similar funding arrangement over unvested or escrowed plan securities is expressly prohibited conduct for any holder.
rules.evidence: a margin loan or similar funding arrangement or other financial transaction which can give rise to pledging, lending or using the securities as collateral

rules.detail: Once vested and out of escrow, a margin loan over the relevant securities is permitted with clearance under 5.3/5.4, applicable to any holder regardless of Designated Person status.
rules.evidence: After vesting and the cessation of any applicable escrow arrangements, a holder of the relevant securities may undertake any transaction of a type referred to in this section provided they obtain written clearance

rules.detail: Acquiring or disposing of Imricor securities in connection with 'other security arrangement' (i.e. granting security) is expressly Trading, permitted for general personnel subject to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Trading in securities includes: ... acquiring or disposing of Imricor securities in connection with margin lending or other security arrangement

rules.detail: Granting security over Imricor securities by a Designated Person requires the same year-round prior written clearance as any other Trading.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may trade in Imricor securities outside of Blackout Periods if they obtain prior written clearance

rules.detail: Using unvested or escrowed plan securities as collateral, or otherwise pledging them, is expressly prohibited conduct for any holder.
rules.evidence: a margin loan or similar funding arrangement or other financial transaction which can give rise to pledging, lending or using the securities as collateral

rules.detail: Once vested and out of escrow, granting security over the relevant securities is permitted with 5.3/5.4 clearance, regardless of Designated Person status.
rules.evidence: After vesting and the cessation of any applicable escrow arrangements, a holder of the relevant securities may undertake any transaction of a type referred to in this section provided they obtain written clearance

rules.detail: Any financing 'in connection with' Imricor securities (margin lending or other security arrangement) is expressly Trading, permitted for general personnel subject to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Trading in securities includes: ... acquiring or disposing of Imricor securities in connection with margin lending or other security arrangement

rules.detail: Secured financing Trading by Designated Persons requires the same year-round prior written clearance as any other Trading.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may trade in Imricor securities outside of Blackout Periods if they obtain prior written clearance

rules.detail: Any financial transaction over unvested or escrowed plan securities that gives rise to pledging, lending, using as collateral, or a margin loan/similar funding arrangement, is expressly prohibited for any holder - the broadest of the topic bans and directly covers a secured collar loan.
rules.evidence: a margin loan or similar funding arrangement or other financial transaction which can give rise to pledging, lending or using the securities as collateral

rules.detail: Once vested and out of escrow, secured financing arrangements over the relevant securities are permitted with 5.3/5.4 clearance, applicable to any holder including non-Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: After vesting and the cessation of any applicable escrow arrangements, a holder of the relevant securities may undertake any transaction of a type referred to in this section provided they obtain written clearance

rules.detail: No Designated Person may trade on a short-term basis, defined as less than three months; no carve-outs are stated.
rules.evidence: no Designated Person may trade in Imricor securities on a short-term basis. Short-term means less than three months.

rules.detail: The short-term trading ban is expressly confined to Designated Persons; general Imricor Personnel are not restricted by it.

clearance.evidence: Imricor Personnel must not trade in Imricor securities when they possess inside information
for trading by directors of Imricor - from the Chairman ... the relevant trading must occur within the 7 days beginning on the day after the clearance.
for trading by the Chairman - from the Board

clearance.tier: employees (Designated Persons who are not directors)
clearance.evidence: for trading by employees (who are not also directors) - from the Chief Executive Officer

clearance.approver: Chairman (or Board if Chairman absent or trading)
clearance.evidence: Designated Persons may trade in Imricor securities during a Blackout Period with: (a) the prior written clearance of the Chairman; or (b) if the Chairman is absent ... the prior written clearance of the Board, if one of the following exceptional circumstances applies

short_term.evidence: no Designated Person may trade in Imricor securities on a short-term basis. Short-term means less than three months.

exceptions.evidence: acquire Imricor's ordinary shares by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to ordinary shares
acquire Imricor securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire Imricor securities under a dividend reinvestment plan, a rights issue or a share purchase plan that is available to all holders of securities of the same class
dispose of rights acquired under a rights issue of a kind referred to in paragraph (c) above
acquire, or agree to acquire, options or other rights under an Imricor's equity incentive plan

exercise options or other rights acquired under an Imricor's equity incentive plan (but may not sell all or part of the shares received upon exercise of the options other than in accordance with this policy)
transfer Imricor securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme

invest in, or trade units of, a fund or other scheme where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party provided the Imricor Personnel does not hold more than 5% of the economic value of that fund or other scheme
accept a takeover offer or an equal access buy-back
effect transactions in Imricor securities pursuant to approved trading plans established under Rule 10b5-1 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (US), as amended.

if the Designated Person is facing severe financial hardship (as determined by the relevant decision maker approving the clearance) and can only meet their financial commitments by selling their securities

if the Designated Persons is required by a court order, a court enforceable undertaking (eg. a bona fide family settlement), or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to transfer, or accept a transfer, of Imricor securities
such other exceptional circumstances as may from time to time be determined by the Chairman or Board (as applicable)

exemption_authority: Chairman (or Board if the Chairman is absent or trading) decides exceptional-circumstances clearance to trade during a Blackout Period (5.2); the Chairman, Board or CEO (per tier) grants or refuses ordinary clearance in their discretion, with or without conditions or reasons, final and binding, and confidential if refused (5.4). The Board may adjust Blackout Periods (5.1).
jurisdiction_overlays: US Securities Exchange Act of 1934, including Rule 10b5-1 trading plans

bespoke_clauses.clause: After vesting and the cessation of any applicable escrow arrangements, a holder of the relevant securities may undertake any transaction of a type referred to in this section provided they obtain written clearance in the manner described in sections 5.3 and 5.4 and comply with all applicable laws (including insider trading laws) and the other provisions of this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This extends the Designated-Person-style clearance regime (Chairman/Board/CEO approval, 7-day validity, confidential and unreviewable refusal) to every holder of vested former-plan securities, not just Designated Persons, so a funded collar over an executive's vested equity always needs prior written clearance regardless of the executive's seniority.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Prohibited conduct includes writing forward contracts or put or call options over the underlying securities, trading in derivative products or entering into other arrangements intended to hedge a "profit" in those securities, a margin loan or similar funding arrangement or other financial transaction which can give rise to pledging, lending or using the securities as collateral.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single clause names, almost verbatim, every component of a funded collar (put, call, derivative trading, margin loan, pledge/collateral) and bans all of them outright while the underlying plan securities are unvested or in escrow, with no clearance route at all - the collar can only be built once vesting and escrow have ended.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may trade in Imricor securities outside of Blackout Periods if they obtain prior written clearance as follows: (a) for trading by directors of Imricor - from the Chairman; (b) for trading by the Chairman - from the Board; and (c) for trading by employees (who are not also directors) - from the Chief Executive Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike policies that only require pre-clearance during closed periods, IMR requires Designated Persons to obtain prior written clearance for every trade, year-round, so a director or KMP entering a funded collar needs Chairman/Board/CEO sign-off even in an otherwise open period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The clearance may be given or refused by the Clearance Officer in their discretion, with or without conditions, and with or without giving any reasons. A decision to refuse clearance is final and binding on the Designated Person, and the Designated Person must keep the decision and any reasons given confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If clearance for the collar or its loan leg is refused, there is no appeal and the executive cannot disclose the refusal (including, on its face, to the bank), which constrains how a declined deal can be discussed or restructured.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where clearance is given, the relevant trading must occur within the 7 days beginning on the day after the clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar (or its unwind) must be priced and executed within 7 days of clearance, requiring tight coordination between the executive, the company and the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance to trade will not be granted if the Clearance Officer believes that Imricor is likely in the short term to release a periodic financial report or other financial data, or make an announcement of market sensitive information under ASX Listing Rule 3.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance for collar entry, adjustment or unwind can be refused even outside the formal Blackout Periods if an announcement is imminent, adding timing uncertainty beyond the fixed windows.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under this policy, but only over vested, non-escrowed Imricor securities and only with prior written clearance. Section 6.2 expressly bans writing forward contracts, put or call options, other derivative trading, margin loans and any pledging or use-as-collateral of plan securities that remain unvested or subject to escrow, with no exception - so the collar cannot be written, and the loan cannot be secured, until vesting and escrow have ended. Once vested and unrestricted, the same clause expressly permits these transactions for any holder, Designated Person or not, provided prior written clearance is obtained under sections 5.3/5.4 (Chairman for directors, Board for the Chairman, CEO for other employees), clearance is executed within 7 days, and the holder is not in possession of inside information. Designated Persons face a further blanket requirement to obtain clearance for all trading year-round (not just in Blackout Periods) and are banned from trading with a view to a holding period under three months, so the collar's tenor and entry timing must be planned around clearance windows, the three Blackout Periods, and the risk of an imminent-announcement clearance refusal. Clearance refusals are final, unreviewable and must be kept confidential, so there is no fallback if the Chairman, Board or CEO declines to approve the arrangement.
